# Tier-2 Dependencies - Require Manual Review Before Merge
#
# Criteria (any match triggers tier-2):
# - New direct dependencies (not transitive)
# - Handles: network/IO, cryptography, unsafe code, financial data
# - Repo signals: <100 GitHub stars, unmaintained (>1yr), single maintainer
#
# Format:
#   crate           - tier-2, any version change needs review
#   crate=x.y.z     - PINNED, exact version required
#
# Pinned entries include: # review-date | risk-factors
# The auto-merge workflow reads this file and applies 'tier-2' label.
# The "tier-2 pins" CI job (.github/scripts/check-tier2-pins.sh) enforces that every PINNED
# entry above matches the `=` requirement in every manifest declaring that crate, so a bump
# cannot land while leaving this record behind. CI cannot verify that the re-verification a
# pinned entry mandates was actually performed — only that this file was not left untouched.

ibapi=4.1.0  # 2026-09-14 | Financial protocol, community-maintained, no official SDK. Reviewed 3.2.0->3.3.0, all four properties recorded at 3.2.0 re-verified and still hold: zero unsafe (also no transmute/from_raw/extern "C"/asm!; holds by inspection, not by lint — upstream has no #![forbid(unsafe_code)]), no build.rs, dependency tree byte-identical vs 3.2.0 (both Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock differ by the version line alone; 9 direct deps under our `default-features = false, features = ["sync"]` selection, unchanged), still only a caller-supplied TWS socket (reconnect reuses the caller's address — no fallback host, no telemetry) + the opt-in local recorder dir (IBAPI_RECORDING_DIR; recorder.rs byte-identical). Env set unchanged (IBAPI_RECORDING_DIR, IBAPI_TIMEZONE_ALIASES); no process spawn, no obfuscation; published from git b140b312d1136d240f3b5651a89f4778e01aa222.
#   New in 3.3.0, reviewed: `src/config` — despite the name it reads NO local files and NO env vars. It wraps two TWS wire messages (ReqConfig=108/UpdateConfig=109) over the already-open socket, whose protobuf types already existed in 3.2.0. Version-gated, #[must_use] builder, not reachable during connect/handshake.
#   NOTE (capability, not vulnerability): `update_config()` can write the gateway's own safety settings — read_only_api, the bypass_* order precautions, trusted_ips, allow_localhost_only, socket_port, master_client_id. rustrade does not call it and does not re-export it; keep it out of the wrapper surface unless there is a deliberate reason.
#   Upstream BREAKING in a minor release: the `fundamental` module was removed (IBKR retired reqFundamentalData in TWS API 10.47). rustrade never used it — verified no reference to fundamental_data / FundamentalData / FundamentalReportType / TickType::FundamentalRatios.
#   The serde-xml-rs/xml-rs note at rustrade-data/Cargo.toml is UNCHANGED and still accurate: they are build-deps of time-tz (non-optional dep of ibapi, timezone codegen), single path each, never linked into the binary. Removing `fundamental` did not and could not drop them — ibapi never had a direct XML dependency.
#   ORDER WIRE FORMAT audited (3.x places orders via protobuf only, so the proto path IS the order wire): the entire encoder delta is 2 lines — `hedge_max_size` (new tag 144) and `deactivate`. Both go through `some_bool`/Option, which omit the field on the default value, so the bytes sent for any order rustrade builds today are byte-identical to 3.2.0. market_data/contracts encoders are byte-identical.
#   3.3.0 rolls up 3.2.1's transport rework, which is NOT fully described in the upstream changelog. Request-less TWS errors (id == -1) outside the 2100..=2169 warning range — which includes the connectivity codes 1100/1101/1102/1300 — now fail in-flight one-shot requests instead of hanging, and the sync shared-queue drain in `send_shared_request` makes concurrent callers of the SAME one-shot API able to discard each other's response. NEITHER REACHES US: rustrade calls none of the affected one-shot APIs (next_valid_order_id, managed_accounts, server_time, family_codes, market_rule, market_depth_exchanges, news_providers, scanner_parameters, wsh_metadata). `client.next_order_id()` is a different method — a local counter increment, byte-identical across the two versions, not a request. Re-check this if the wrapper ever starts calling one of those.
#   NOT VERIFIABLE OFF-GATEWAY: the handshake now advertises server version 225 (was 221), so a modern TWS may negotiate the 222/224 field layouts. No decoder branches on them. The ibkr integration tests are all #[ignore]d (they need a live TWS), so this bump has NOT been exercised against a real gateway — do that before relying on it in production.
#   Other additive breaks that cost us nothing, verified: TickType gained 6 odd-lot variants and lost FundamentalRatios=47 (explicit discriminants, so no renumbering; our quotes.rs matches use `_` fallbacks), and `Order` gained 2 public fields (we build orders with `..Order::default()`).
#
# Re-verified against the vendored =4.0.1 source on 2026-09-16 (3.3.0 -> 4.0.1). A MAJOR bump, so
# every property this entry mandates was re-checked rather than spot-checked. Published from git
# b05574806d153b1ca304d9d2905c9ca3015727eb (3.3.0 was b140b312d1136d240f3b5651a89f4778e01aa222).
#
# ORDER WIRE FORMAT: unchanged, and provably so. `src/orders/common/encoders.rs` -- the whole
# outbound order encoder -- is BYTE-IDENTICAL to 3.3.0, md5 049bed6ba1d842eedeb81ec639852583. The
# 4.0 order-side churn is all decode and routing: `OrderStatusKind` gained `Unknown(String)`, and
# order-bound notices were reclassified. Nothing this crate sends to TWS changed shape.
#
# The four standing properties all still hold:
#   1. ZERO unsafe -- 0 real constructs in both versions, and no `transmute`, `from_raw`,
#      `extern "C"` or `asm!` anywhere in `src/`. Still by inspection, not by lint: upstream has no
#      #![forbid(unsafe_code)].
#   2. NO build.rs -- still absent.
#   3. DEPENDENCY TREE -- `[dependencies]` is byte-for-byte identical to 3.3.0 under our
#      `default-features = false, features = ["sync"]` selection. The only manifest deltas are the
#      version line, one new example (`replay_raw_capture`), and two DEV-dependencies we never
#      compile (serial_test 3.1.1 -> 4.0.1, temp-env gains the `async_closure` feature).
#   4. NETWORK SURFACE -- still only the caller-supplied TWS socket. No new hosts: the URL set in
#      `src/` is identical to 3.3.0 and is entirely doc links. No process spawn, no telemetry, no
#      obfuscation.
#
# ENV SURFACE CHANGED -- one addition, opt-in: `IBAPI_RAW_CAPTURE_DIR` joins `IBAPI_RECORDING_DIR`
# and `IBAPI_TIMEZONE_ALIASES`. Set it to a directory and every connection writes a byte-for-byte
# copy of the inbound socket stream, length prefixes included, to local disk. CAPABILITY NOTE, not a
# vulnerability: those captures are UNREDACTED wire bytes, so they carry account ids, positions and
# orders in the clear, and an unwritable path now warns and disables the tap rather than panicking
# during `Client::connect`. Unset here and never set by rustrade; treat any capture directory as
# credential-adjacent if it is ever turned on for debugging.
#
# TRANSPORT REWORK, re-audited because this entry mandates it. Broader than 3.2.1's: routing.rs,
# sync.rs, async.rs, common.rs and recorder.rs all changed, and raw_capture.rs is new. The parts
# that reach rustrade:
#   a. NOTICE RECLASSIFICATION, and it is the one change here with a behavioural effect the
#      compiler cannot catch. `is_warning_message` now classifies code 0 and the `Warning:` form of
#      code 399 as warnings, and `classify_error` routes a warning owned by a request-bound
#      subscription as a non-terminal `RoutedItem::Notice` instead of a stream-ending
#      `RoutedItem::Error`. `iter_data()`/`timeout_iter_data()` DROP notices. So a held-until-RTH
#      399 no longer closes a `place_order` subscription: it is dropped, the subscription stays
#      open, and the following `OrderStatus(PreSubmitted)` now arrives there. The 399 form WITHOUT a
#      `Warning:` line still surfaces as `Err(Error::Notice)`. Both paths are handled and documented
#      at `INFORMATIONAL_ORDER_CODES` in rustrade-execution/src/client/ibkr/mod.rs.
#   b. Frame validation: a 4-byte length prefix that cannot describe a TWS message (under the
#      message-id width, or over the official 16 MiB `Constants.MaxMsgSize` cap) now raises
#      `Error::InvalidFrame` and drives a reconnect, where 3.3.0 would size an allocation from it.
#      Classified as `is_connection_lost`, so both dispatchers reconnect. Strictly a hardening.
#   c. One-shot requests now narrow the inbound frame to the message type they asked for before
#      decoding, and retry-on-connection-reset is uniform (at most three attempts) across the
#      one-shots that previously had none or had unbounded retries. We call none of the affected
#      one-shot APIs -- the 3.3.0 note in this entry lists them and that list is unchanged.
#   d. Code 202 (cancel confirmation) is now a non-terminal notice on request-bound subscriptions
#      rather than the `Err` that used to end a `cancel_order` subscription. DOES NOT REACH US:
#      every `cancel_order` call site drops the returned subscription without iterating it.
#
# Consumer-side API churn this bump required (recorded so the next bump knows the shape):
# `OrderStatusKind` gained `Unknown(String)` and lost `Copy`; historical tick sizes moved from `i32`
# to `Option<f64>` (`TickLast.size`, `TickBidAsk.size_bid`/`size_ask`), which is a real fix -- the
# old `i32` parse truncated a fractional crypto size of `0.5` to `0`; and `option_chain` became a
# builder with `exchange` as a setter.
#
# NOT VERIFIABLE OFF-GATEWAY, and stronger than at 3.3.0 because this is a major bump touching the
# transport: the ibkr integration tests are all #[ignore]d (they need a live TWS), and CI does not
# run them. NOTHING has exercised 4.0.1's handshake, order path, reconnect loop or the reclassified
# notice routing against a real gateway. The notice change in (a) in particular alters what a
# `place_order` subscription observes for a held order, and only a live out-of-RTH placement can
# confirm the `OrderStatus(PreSubmitted)` actually arrives where this bump implies it will. Do that
# before relying on 4.0.1 in production.
#
# Re-verified against the vendored =4.1.0 source on 2026-09-22 (4.0.1 -> 4.1.0). Published from git
# 2dfc49bef73d12f0a3363ea91256d86a77cb9b6f (4.0.1 was b05574806d153b1ca304d9d2905c9ca3015727eb).
# The maintainer's author email changed domain (wsbsolutions.com -> wsblabs.com); same name, same
# crates.io publisher, recorded because it is the only identity-adjacent delta in the manifest.
#
# ORDER WIRE FORMAT: unchanged, and more strongly than at 4.0.1. `src/orders/common/encoders.rs` is
# BYTE-IDENTICAL, md5 049bed6ba1d842eedeb81ec639852583 -- the same hash this entry recorded at 4.0.1
# and 3.3.0. ALL 16 encoder files in the crate are byte-identical. There is no encoder delta to
# enumerate. Nothing this crate sends to TWS changed shape.
#
# The four standing properties all still hold:
#   1. ZERO unsafe -- 0 constructs in `src/` in both versions, no transmute/from_raw/extern "C"/asm!.
#      The one new `forget(` grep hit is tokio's safe `SemaphorePermit::forget` at
#      connection/async_tests.rs:390 -- async AND #[cfg(test)], doubly not ours. Still by inspection,
#      not by lint: upstream has no #![forbid(unsafe_code)].
#   2. NO build.rs -- still absent; `build = false` explicit at Cargo.toml:16.
#   3. DEPENDENCY TREE -- `[dependencies]` byte-for-byte identical under our
#      `default-features = false, features = ["sync"]` selection: md5 4b001df77c55c0bf51077d4b661d6ee5
#      over everything from `[dependencies.` onward, identical in both. `[features]` and the 139
#      `[[example]]` targets identical. THE ENTIRE MANIFEST DELTA IS TWO LINES: version and author
#      email. No dev-dependency delta this time, unlike 4.0.1. The serde-xml-rs (0.5.1) / xml-rs
#      (0.8.28) note is UNCHANGED and still accurate: build-deps of time-tz 2.0.0, itself a
#      non-optional dep of ibapi.
#   4. NETWORK SURFACE -- still only the caller-supplied TWS socket. URL host set identical and
#      entirely doc links; the sole textual URL delta in the tree is a trailing `.` after a
#      tick_types.html link. No new hosts, no process spawn, no telemetry, no obfuscation.
#
# ENV SURFACE UNCHANGED -- the same three, same sites: IBAPI_RECORDING_DIR (recorder.rs:34),
# IBAPI_TIMEZONE_ALIASES (common/timezone/mod.rs:148), IBAPI_RAW_CAPTURE_DIR (raw_capture.rs:93). No
# new tap of the unredacted-capture class. The 4.0.1 note on IBAPI_RAW_CAPTURE_DIR carrying account
# ids, positions and orders in the clear stands as written.
#
# NOTICE RECLASSIFICATION, re-audited because this entry mandates it -- and this time it DOES reach a
# live path.
#   `is_warning_message` is BYTE-IDENTICAL (messages.rs:1102-1106 -> 1108-1112). What moved is the
#   constant it reads: WARNING_CODE_RANGE 2100..=2169 -> 2100..=2199, because IB kept adding warnings
#   above the published ceiling (2176, 2187) and each was a hard error.
#   `classify_error` (routing.rs:215) swapped its predicate from the deleted `is_warning_error` to
#   `messages::is_informational_code` (messages.rs:1119), now the single owner of the precedence chain.
#   The routing-informational set changed STRICTLY ADDITIVELY:
#     4.0.1: is_warning_message U {2188,10089,10090,10167} U {202}
#     4.1.0: {202} U {317,2188,10089,10090,10091,10167} U is_warning_message(now ..=2199)
#            U {1100,1101,1102,1300}
#   i.e. +317, +10091, +2170..=2199, +the system codes. NOTHING was removed -- no frame that was
#   informational in 4.0.1 becomes an error in 4.1.0. `Notice::category()` also moved
#   DATA_ADVISORY_CODES ahead of the warning and order-rejection bands; that reorder is
#   ROUTING-NEUTRAL (the set is a union either way) and only changes the reported variant for 317
#   (OrderRejection -> DataAdvisory) and 2188 (Warning -> DataAdvisory).
#   a. OUR ORDER HANDLING IS UNAFFECTED. INFORMATIONAL_ORDER_CODES = &[399] at
#      rustrade-execution/src/client/ibkr/mod.rs, and 399 is in neither the new advisory list nor the
#      system list, so BOTH forms classify exactly as in 4.0.1: with a `Warning:` line -> warning ->
#      non-terminal Notice dropped by timeout_iter_data, subscription stays open; without one -> falls
#      to ORDER_REJECTION_CODE_RANGE -> Err(Error::Notice), still matched against the list. That
#      rustdoc has been updated to record the re-verification and to carve 202/317 out of its
#      "whole 200..=399 range" sentence, which was no longer exact.
#   b. MARKET DEPTH 317 -- the one live-path change that reached us, and it was a LOSS OF
#      OBSERVABILITY. FIXED IN THIS PR rather than deferred. rustrade-data/src/exchange/ibkr/mod.rs
#      iterated `sub.iter_data()`, which DROPS notices. Under 4.0.1 a 317 ("Market depth data has been
#      RESET") was an OrderRejection -> Err -> the loop logged, sent DataError::Socket and broke, so
#      the consumer resubscribed and rebuilt the book. Under 4.1.0 it is a DataAdvisory ->
#      informational -> Notice -> silently dropped, and DepthAggregator would have kept applying rows
#      to a book it never cleared while TWS had discarded its own. ibapi's behaviour is the CORRECT
#      one and it documents the consumer contract at market_data/realtime/mod.rs:253-259 ("drop every
#      row held and rebuild from the updates that follow"); rustrade did not implement it, so 4.0.1
#      was fail-loud only by accident. The loop now iterates `sub.iter()` and matches
#      SubscriptionItem::Notice, calling the new `DepthAggregator::on_venue_reset` on code 317 --
#      which empties both sides, ADVANCES the sequence (reusing `clear()` would have renumbered to 0
#      and a consumer ordering by sequence would have read the emptied book as older than the stale
#      one it replaces) and returns the emptied snapshot so it is forwarded at once. Non-317 notices
#      are logged at warn!, preserving what iter_data() did. Its sibling 316 (HALTED) stays terminal
#      and is still handled by the error arm.
#   c. SYSTEM CODES 1100/1101/1102/1300 no longer fail in-flight one-shots (this reverses part of
#      3.2.1's rework). DOES NOT REACH US, and the reason is structural:
#      ErrorDisposition::NoticeAndFailOneShots calls only `shared_channels.fail_one_shot_channels(...)`
#      (transport/sync.rs:452, identical to 4.0.1's :401) -- the shared-channel registry, never
#      request-id-bound subscriptions. rustrade has 0 call sites for all nine shared one-shots this
#      entry has listed since 3.3.0 (re-verified: each 0). `contract_details`, which we DO call, is
#      request-id-bound and was never on that path.
#
# CONSUMER-SIDE API CHURN: none forced by the compiler. `OrderUpdate` gained `OrderBound(OrderBound)`
# and the changelog says exhaustive matches must handle it; our match in
# rustrade-execution/src/client/ibkr/mod.rs ends with `_ => None`, so it compiles unchanged.
# `DATA_ADVISORY_CODES: [i32;4]` became `&[i32]` -- we never reference it (0 hits, as for
# WARNING_CODE_RANGE, NoticeCategory, SYSTEM_MESSAGE_CODES and the notice stream). The `Orders`
# decoder dropped a dead CommissionsReport arm that would have decoded a commission frame as an open
# order; our open_orders propagates any Err via `?`, so this removes a spurious failure path.
#
# FIXES ON PATHS WE COMPILE, recorded because they are the reason to take this bump:
#   - New ShutdownSignal (transport/sync/shutdown.rs, std Mutex+Condvar, poison-tolerant via
#     unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner), no panic path). Client::drop / disconnect() no longer
#     block until the reconnect backoff exhausts -- forever under reconnect_forever. We call
#     disconnect().
#   - HistoricalDataEnd parsing (market_data/historical/common/decoders/mod.rs:74-100): the old
#     `rsplit_once(' ')` took only the LAST word as the zone, so "China Standard Time" resolved as
#     "Time", failed to parse and ended the subscription; the zone-less UTC form `YYYYMMDD-HH:MM:SS`
#     also failed. Both now parse. We use historical streams heavily.
#   - ORDER-ID GENERATOR, and a wrapper gap this exposes rather than creates: `set`/`reset` became
#     `raise` (fetch_max, client/id_generator.rs:46-53) and a successful reconnect now re-seeds the
#     generator from the handshake's NextValidId, fixing error 103 after a gateway restart. WE DO NOT
#     BENEFIT: connect_sync takes `client.next_order_id()` ONCE into its own Arc<Mutex<i32>> and
#     allocates from that thereafter, never consulting ibapi's generator again. Pre-existing, NOT a
#     regression -- but 4.1.0 is the first version where deferring to ibapi's generator would be
#     correct, so the wrapper counter could now be retired.
#   - TRANSPORT_RECONNECT_CODE (-8) is broadcast to the notice fan-out after reconnect cleanup; we do
#     not consume the notice stream, so it is a no-op here. NOTICE_STREAM_LAG_CODE (-7) is
#     #[cfg(feature = "async")] and is not compiled for us at all.
#
# LOCKFILE: 4 changed lines, all in the ibapi package block (version + checksum). ZERO packages added,
# ZERO removed, measured by counting +/- `name =` lines in the PR diff.
# RUSTSEC not verified offline -- no local advisory-db; CI's cargo-deny job covers it.
#
# NOT VERIFIABLE OFF-GATEWAY, unchanged in force from 4.0.1: the ibkr integration tests are all
# #[ignore]d (20 in rustrade-data/tests/ibkr_integration.rs) and CI does not run them. NOTHING has
# exercised 4.1.0's handshake, its shutdown-aware reconnect backoff, the order-id re-seed, the widened
# 2100..=2199 warning band, the 317/10091 advisory routing or the new HistoricalDataEnd parser against
# a real gateway. THE 317 FIX IN (b) IS UNIT-TESTED ONLY -- `on_venue_reset` has three tests, but no
# test drives a real 317 notice through the subscription loop, because that needs a live level-2
# subscription that receives a book reset. Do that before relying on 4.1.0 in production.
binance-sdk=70.1.0  # 2026-09-14 | Exchange SDK, signing/IO. PINNED: margin user-data stream couples to 3 `binance_sdk::common` internals (lower-stability than the public per-market API). ANY bump MUST re-verify all 3 before merge:
#   1. common::websocket::WebsocketApi::send_message      — signature + WebsocketMessageSendOptions signing fields (margin WS subscribe send)
#   2. ws.common.events.subscribe (WebsocketEventEmitter) — receive/event-callback path (margin WS event delivery)
#   3. common::utils::send_request                        — signature + HMAC signing + X-MBX-APIKEY header (hand-rolled `userListenToken` POST; SDK binds no endpoint for it)
# Background: legacy margin listen-key user-data API retired 2026-02-20; SDK binds only the dead endpoint, so the live `userListenToken` flow is hand-rolled atop these internals.
#
# Re-verified against the vendored =69.1.0 source on 2026-09-14 (60.0.0 -> 69.1.0, nine majors). All 3 still hold,
# and the strongest evidence is that they cannot have changed: `common/websocket.rs` is BYTE-IDENTICAL between
# 60.0.0 and 69.1.0 (md5 38b5990bb85497fdbcec39984732509b), as are common/{mod,config,models}.rs. The only file
# that differs in `common/` is utils.rs, and its entire delta is `build_user_agent` plus that function's tests.
#   1. `send_message(&self, method: &str, payload: BTreeMap<String, Value>,
#      options: WebsocketMessageSendOptions) -> Result<SendWebsocketMessageResult<R>, WebsocketError>`
#      — shape unchanged (websocket.rs:1630); WebsocketMessageSendOptions still carries exactly
#      with_api_key / is_signed / is_session_logon / is_session_logout. Both margin WS call sites still match.
#   2. `WebsocketEventEmitter::subscribe` (websocket.rs:125) still spawns exactly one task per subscription
#      draining an unbounded channel via a sequential `while let Some(event) = rx.recv().await` loop, so the
#      FnMut is invoked sequentially. That is precisely the contract the non-atomic `Option::take()`
#      in the margin `account_stream` callback relies on for soundness.
#   3. `send_request(configuration, endpoint, method, query_params, body_params, time_unit, is_signed)`
#      — 7-arg shape unchanged (utils.rs:841); `is_signed` still injects `timestamp` (:857-858), signs via
#      `configuration.signature_gen.get_signature(...)` (:866-870), appends `signature` to the query string
#      (:887-889), and sets `X-MBX-APIKEY` (:923-925). The hand-rolled `POST /sapi/v1/userListenToken` is
#      therefore still signed as intended.
#
# Dependency surface: `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]` and `[build-dependencies]` are byte-for-byte
# identical across all nine majors. The only manifest change is the removal of the `nft` feature (30 -> 29);
# `spot` and `margin_trading` are unchanged and still mean the same thing. No new or removed deps, no MSRV
# change (neither version declares `rust-version`), no new duplicate majors, `anyhow` still the public error
# type. build.rs is identical (6 lines, stamps RUSTC_VERSION). The version number tracks Binance's REST
# surface, not dependency churn — which is why nine majors cost nothing here.
#
# Security: PASS. 60.0.0 has 0 `unsafe`; 69.1.0 has 10, ALL inside `#[cfg(test)]` (utils.rs:1382-1432,
# `env::set_var`/`remove_var`, which edition 2024 requires be wrapped in `unsafe`). Credentials: hand-written
# REDACTING `Debug` on every secret-bearing struct, zero `Serialize` in config.rs. Network hosts: one added
# (`wss://nbstream.binance.com`, behind the `alpha` feature, which we do not enable), one removed (NFT).
# Filesystem: one `read_to_string` of the caller's own PEM. No process exec, no obfuscation. Publisher
# unchanged. Git commits: 60.0.0 = 8cfe7d023236280e9356f84a8c4a12eff558d4aa,
# 69.1.0 = 56a82d787bfc0fc5e321691fdfdbe2b6767f1f0b.
#
# Two findings recorded, neither blocking, both worth knowing before enabling verbose tracing:
#   a. NEW env read `BINANCE_CONNECTOR_RUST_USER_AGENT` (utils.rs:395), regex-gated to binance-cli/binance-skill
#      shapes. The `[^;()]+` character classes admit \r and \n, and the resulting UA is applied via
#      `.parse().unwrap()` (utils.rs:921) — so a crafted value PANICS on HeaderValue parse. That is a DoS, not
#      header injection, and it requires control of the process environment. We never set this variable.
#   b. PRE-EXISTING and NOT a regression (identical in both versions): websocket.rs:1665 logs
#      `debug!("Sending message to WebSocket API: {:?}", request)` — the full signed WS request INCLUDING
#      `apiKey` and `signature` — at DEBUG level. `api_secret` is never logged. Anything enabling DEBUG tracing
#      for this crate will put short-lived credentials in its logs.
#
# Consumer-side API churn this bump required (recorded so the next bump knows the shape): binance-sdk now
# generates a typed enum per endpoint parameter where it used to take `String` (`isIsolated`, order `type`,
# `sideEffectType`), and a distinct response struct per endpoint where `allOrders` and `openOrders` used to
# share one. The enums are wire-identical to the strings they replace (`TRUE`/`FALSE`, `LIMIT`, ...), so the
# migration is behaviour-preserving; they derive no `PartialEq`, so assertions compare `as_str()`.
#
# Record gap, noted so the shape of the miss is not repeated: this entry read `=52.0.0` until
# 2026-09-13 while the manifest had already moved to `=55.0.0` (aefb55b) and then `=60.0.0` (7d8d081).
# Both were plain Dependabot bumps that changed `rustrade-execution/Cargo.toml` without touching this
# file, so the re-verification this entry mandates was never recorded for either. The 2026-09-13 check
# closed that gap at 60.0.0 and this one carries it forward to 69.1.0. The hard `=` pin in the manifest is
# the enforcement; this file is the record. They must move together, and a bump that edits only the
# manifest has skipped a required step.

#
# Re-verified against the vendored =69.2.3 source on 2026-09-16 (69.1.0 -> 69.2.3). All 3 internals
# still hold, and 1 and 2 hold by construction: `common/websocket.rs` is again BYTE-IDENTICAL
# (md5 38b5990bb85497fdbcec39984732509b, the same hash this entry recorded at 69.1.0 and 60.0.0).
# Only TWO files in `common/` differ at all: constants.rs and utils.rs.
#   1. `send_message` — websocket.rs unchanged, so the signature and the four
#      WebsocketMessageSendOptions fields (with_api_key / is_signed / is_session_logon /
#      is_session_logout) are unchanged. Both margin WS call sites still match.
#   2. `WebsocketEventEmitter::subscribe` — websocket.rs unchanged, so the one-task-per-subscription
#      sequential `while let Some(event) = rx.recv().await` drain is intact. That is the contract the
#      non-atomic `Option::take()` in the margin `account_stream` callback relies on for soundness.
#   3. `send_request` — 7-arg shape unchanged (utils.rs:951). Still injects `timestamp`, signs via
#      `configuration.signature_gen.get_signature(...)` (utils.rs:980 — the URL-ENCODED variant,
#      unchanged), appends `signature` to the query string, and sets `X-MBX-APIKEY`. The hand-rolled
#      `POST /sapi/v1/userListenToken` is therefore still signed as intended.
#
# BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, recorded because it is invisible in the changelog and it is on a path we could
# one day take: `build_websocket_api_message` (utils.rs:1304, non-test) changed how it signs a
# SIGNED WebSocket frame — 69.1.0 used `get_signature(&sorted, None)` over the URL-encoded payload,
# 69.2.3 uses the new `get_signature_unencoded(&sorted)` over the plain payload. Binance's WS API
# signs the plain payload, so this is a genuine fix, not a regression. IT DOES NOT REACH US: both
# our `send_message` call sites pass `WebsocketMessageSendOptions::new()`, i.e. unsigned and with no
# API key — the listen token is the sole auth on those frames — so the `is_signed` branch is
# unreachable from rustrade. Re-check this the day any WS frame here sets `is_signed: true`; 69.2.3
# is the first version where that path signs correctly.
#
# Security: PASS, and marginally improved. The new `build_plain_query_string` validates every key
# and value through `ensure_safe_plain_query_component` (utils.rs:625), rejecting `&`, `=` and ASCII
# control characters rather than letting them be spliced unescaped into a signature payload.
# `get_signature` itself is unchanged in behaviour; it was only refactored to share a new private
# `sign_payload`. Real `unsafe` constructs: 10 in BOTH versions, all `std::env::set_var`/`remove_var`
# at utils.rs:1492-1542, all below the `#[cfg(test)]` at utils.rs:1353. (A bare `\bunsafe\b` grep
# reports 10 -> 17; the 7 extra are the word "unsafe" inside the new validator's error strings and
# doc comments, the same over-count caveat this file already records for `dbn`.)
#
# Dependency surface: `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]` and `[build-dependencies]` byte-for-byte
# identical to 69.1.0. build.rs identical. New `stocks` feature (and with it the constants
# STOCKS_REST_API_PROD_URL and a new WS host `wss://nbstream.binance.com/equity`) — we enable only
# `spot` and `margin_trading`, so none of it is compiled. No consumer-side API churn: this bump needs
# no code change, unlike 60.0.0 -> 69.1.0.
#
# Re-verified against the vendored =70.1.0 source on 2026-09-22 (69.2.3 -> 70.1.0). A MAJOR bump,
# and the cheapest one this entry has ever recorded: THE ENTIRE `src/` DELTA IS TWO MODULES WE DO
# NOT COMPILE. `diff -rq` over src/ returns 15 entries, all under
# derivatives_trading_portfolio_margin/ and derivatives_trading_usds_futures/, both

# selection. `src/common/`, `src/spot/`, `src/margin_trading/` and `src/lib.rs` are ALL
# BYTE-IDENTICAL (diff -rq empty on each).
# All 3 internals therefore hold BY CONSTRUCTION: `common/websocket.rs` md5 is again
# 38b5990bb85497fdbcec39984732509b -- the same hash recorded at 60.0.0, 69.1.0 and 69.2.3, now ten
# majors unchanged -- and `common/utils.rs` (1541c46b7c5ba4f5f7ef57286c99695d) did not move either,
# so unlike 69.2.3 not even one file in common/ differs. Quoted from the 70.1.0 source anyway:
#   1. `send_message(&self, method: &str, payload: BTreeMap<String, Value>,
#      options: WebsocketMessageSendOptions) -> Result<SendWebsocketMessageResult<R>, WebsocketError>`
#      (websocket.rs:1630); WebsocketMessageSendOptions (websocket.rs:1404-1409) still carries exactly
#      with_api_key / is_signed / is_session_logon / is_session_logout. Both margin WS call sites
#      (margin.rs:1457, margin.rs:1497) still type-check and both still pass
#      `WebsocketMessageSendOptions::new()`, i.e. unsigned with no API key.
#   2. `WebsocketEventEmitter::subscribe` (websocket.rs:125) still opens an unbounded channel (:129)
#      and spawns exactly ONE task (:137) draining it via a sequential
#      `while let Some(event) = rx.recv().await { callback(event) }` (:138-140). No FuturesUnordered,
#      no per-event spawn, no concurrent dispatch. That is the contract the non-atomic `Option::take()`
#      in the margin `account_stream` callback (margin.rs:1876) relies on for soundness.
#   3. `send_request(configuration, endpoint, method, query_params, body_params, time_unit, is_signed)`
#      -- 7-arg shape unchanged (utils.rs:951-959). `is_signed` still injects `timestamp` (:967-968),
#      signs via `configuration.signature_gen.get_signature(...)` (:979-980), appends `signature` to
#      the query string (:997) and sets `X-MBX-APIKEY` (:1034). The hand-rolled
#      `POST /sapi/v1/userListenToken` (margin.rs:1369) is still signed as intended.
#
# What made it MAJOR, and why it costs us nothing: a pure removal in a module we do not enable.

# Everything else in those two modules is doc-comment rewording. CONSUMER-SIDE API CHURN: NONE.
# rustrade imports only from common/ and margin_trading/ and spot/, all byte-identical, so this bump
# needs no code change. Our `binance_conditional_orders` test is our own spot stop-order test and

parquet  # 2026-07-28 | New direct dep (Parquet decode of provider bulk exports). Reviewed @ 59.1.0 and re-verified @ 59.3.0 (2026-09-13), Apache-2.0, apache/arrow-rs (ASF-governed, ~65M downloads). MUST stay `default-features = false, features = ["zstd"]` — that is what keeps `arrow` out, and re-enabling defaults pulls arrow-array/buffer/data/schema/select/ipc, base64, brotli, flate2, lz4, snap and simdutf8 in one line. Under the pinned feature set: no build.rs; no network, process-spawn or env access anywhere in the library (the only `env::var` is in `src/bin/parquet-fromcsv.rs`, a CLI binary we do not build); 19 `unsafe` sites in the compiled paths, all in columnar decode hot spots (bit packing, RLE, byte-stream-split, bloom filter) and idiomatic for the crate class. Tree is 12 direct deps. Net-new surface, measured by diffing Cargo.lock before/after rather than eyeballed: COMPILED ON ORDINARY TARGETS — seq-macro, twox-hash, libm, num-bigint 0.5 (see below), and a second major of ahash (0.8.12, now built alongside the pre-existing 0.7.8). libm is not a new dependency edge: it arrives because parquet's tree turns on the `libm` feature of the already-present num-traits. LOCKFILE-ONLY — const-random and const-random-macro enter Cargo.lock via ahash 0.8 but are target-gated and absent from `cargo tree` on every target we ship; parquet gates ahash's `compile-time-rng` feature (the only thing that pulls const-random) on `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`, so they build only for wasm32. Re-check them if this workspace ever targets it -- any downstream consumer targeting wasm32 will compile const-random-macro: const-random-macro is a build-time proc-macro pulling getrandom + tiny-keccak, i.e. a compile-time RNG. ALREADY PRESENT, not new — zstd/zstd-safe/zstd-sys, chrono, bytes, hashbrown, half, num-*, getrandom, once_cell, zerocopy, tiny-keccak. Verified the arrow-free column-reader API compiles and decodes real 4-column and 7-column artifacts (370,531 rows) — the feature reduction is real, not theoretical. 59.2.0 dropped the `paste` dependency outright, which retires the RUSTSEC-2024-0436 exception this entry used to carry: `paste` is no longer in Cargo.lock at all, so there is nothing left to accept. 59.2.0 also moved parquet from num-bigint 0.4 to 0.5 (deps: num-integer + num-traits only, no new surface); 0.4.6 remains in the tree for other consumers, which `bans.multiple-versions = "warn"` permits. 59.3.0 changes the dependency set no further — its list is byte-identical to 59.2.0, and no `arrow-*` crate appears anywhere in Cargo.lock. Not pinned — any version bump still needs review, and must re-check that `arrow` has not become non-optional.

databento  # 2026-09-13 | Direct dep (historical + live market data). Meets the criteria above on three counts — network/IO, credential handling (API key via `DATABENTO_API_KEY`), and financial data — but was never listed when it was introduced; this entry closes that gap rather than recording a new dependency. Reviewed @ 0.61.0, Apache-2.0, databento/databento-rs — a first-party vendor SDK, not community-maintained, which is the opposite of the ibapi risk profile above. No build.rs. Zero `unsafe` in the `databento` crate itself. The unsafe lives one level down in `dbn` (0.69.0, Apache-2.0, no build.rs, same vendor), where a grep over src reports 133 occurrences — that count includes `unsafe impl`, `unsafe fn`, blocks and comments alike, so it over-counts distinct sites. They cluster exactly where a zero-copy wire-format decoder puts them: record_ref.rs (25), decode/dbn/fsm.rs (17), record_buf.rs (16), record/conv.rs (8), plus the sync/async encode paths. Idiomatic for the crate class, same justification parquet's 19 sites get. A further 21 occurrences in dbn's python/record.rs are NOT compiled: they sit behind dbn's opt-in `python` feature, and `pyo3` is absent from Cargo.lock — re-check if the feature set ever changes. That surface is not merely theoretical, and this is the reason to keep reading dbn's changelog and not only databento's: 0.61.0 fixes an unsound `AsRef<[u8]>` for `RecordBuf` that could yield a slice longer than the backing buffer, and a metadata count bug that made decoding read into the start of records. Treat dbn bumps as soundness-relevant. 16 direct deps (async-compression, bon, chrono, dbn, futures, hex, reqwest, serde, serde_json, sha2, thiserror, time, tokio, tokio-util, tracing, zstd), all already in the tree. Not pinned — any version bump still needs review.

# Net-new lockfile entries NOT attributable to a tier-2 crate above, recorded so the
# "measured by diffing Cargo.lock" claim in the parquet entry stays true of the whole file:
#
# rand_pcg 0.10.2 — transitive, arrives via the quinn-proto 0.11.14 -> 0.11.16 bump made for
#   RUSTSEC-2026-0185, not via any direct dependency of ours. rust-random org (same maintainers
#   as `rand`, already in tree), MIT/Apache-2.0, zero build.rs, one dependency (rand_core 0.10.1,
#   also already in tree). A PCG generator used by quinn-proto for connection-ID and timing
#   jitter — not a CSPRNG and not used as one; quinn-proto takes its cryptographic randomness
